messages.content:
You are an experienced UK building control surveyor. Answer the question about the work item
in the JSON state. Choose exactly one label:
- not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
- competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
- building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
- full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
Reply with JSON only: {"label": "<one label>", "probabilities": {"<label>": <0..1>, ...}} with a
probability for every label, summing to 1.

Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

{"work_item": "Install a new circuit from the house to a detached garden shed", "project": "House in England", "jurisdiction": "England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.", "clauses": [{"ref": "reg 12(6A)", "document": "BR2010", "text": "(6A) A person intending to carry out building work in relation to which Part P of Schedule 1 imposes a requirement is required to give a building notice or an application for building control approval with full plans where the work consists of— (a) the installation of a new circuit; (b) the replacement of a consumer unit; or (c) any addition or alteration to existing circuits in a special location."}, {"ref": "para 2.8", "document": "ADP2013", "text": "2.8 Installing fixed electrical equipment is within the scope of Part P, even if the final connection is by a standard 13A plug and socket, but is notifiable only if it involves work set out in regulation 12(6A). For example: a. installing a built-in cooker is not notifiable work unless a new cooker circuit is needed b. connecting an electric gate or garage door to an existing isolator switch is not notifiable work, but installing a new circuit from the consumer unit to the isolator is notifiable. Building Regulations 2010 Application of Part P"}, {"ref": "para 2.3", "document": "ADP2013", "text": "2.3 Part P does not apply to electrical installations: a. in business premises in the same building as a dwelling but with separate metering b. that supply the power for lifts in blocks of flats (but Part P does apply to lift installations in single dwellings). NOTE: Schedule 2 to the Building Regulations identifies buildings – for example unoccupied, agricultural, temporary and small detached buildings – that are generally exempt from the requirements of the Regulations. However, conservatories, porches, domestic greenhouses, garages and sheds that share their electricity with a dwelling are not exempt from Part P (by virtue of regulation 9(3)) and must comply with its requirements."}]}

message.content:
A new circuit is notifiable electrical work, and a registered electrician can self-certify it, so the competent person scheme route applies.

- **Part P applies:** under regulation 9(3), sheds that share their electricity with a dwelling are not exempt. So the Schedule 2 exemption for small detached buildings does not remove Part P.
- **It is notifiable:** installing a new circuit is listed in regulation 12(6A)(a), and paragraph 2.8 of Approved Document P confirms this. That rules out not_notifiable.
- **It can be self-certified:** Schedule 3 lists electrical installation work covered by Part P, so a registered competent person can certify it under regul
message.reasoning: This new circuit is notifiable under regulation 12(6A), and since Schedule 3 requires the work be done by a Part P registered competent person, this falls under the competent person scheme route. Since the shed shares electricity with the dwelling, it isn't exempt from these requirements.
